python: enumerate(xs, start=1) gives you a counter that starts at 1.
Run python -m venv .venv to give each project its own packages.
breakpoint() drops you into the debugger at that line.
An f-string like f"{n:,}" formats a number with thousands separators.
A default argument like bucket=[] is created once and shared by every call. Use None instead.
3d-printing: Most failed prints start with the first layer. Clean the bed and level it before changing anything else.
PLA is the easiest filament to start with. PETG is tougher and handles more heat.
Damp filament pops and strings. Store spools in a sealed box with desiccant.
Parts are weakest between layers, so orient a print so the load runs along the layers.
Change one slicer setting at a time, or you will not know what fixed the problem.
woodworking: Wood moves across the grain as humidity changes, so leave solid panels room to expand.
Measure twice, cut once. Better still, mark from the workpiece instead of a ruler when you can.
Sand through the grits in order. Skipping from 80 to 220 leaves scratches that show under finish.
Glue is stronger than the wood on long-grain joints, but weak on end grain.
Wear eye and hearing protection, and keep a push stick next to the table saw.
robotics: The pins on an ESP32 are 3.3 V. Feeding them 5 V signals can damage the board.
Never power motors or servos from a microcontroller pin. Give them their own supply and share the ground.
Use millis() instead of delay() so your sketch can do several things at once.
A floating input reads random values. Use INPUT_PULLUP or add a resistor.
Print to the serial monitor early and often. It is the simplest debugger you have.
data: Look at the raw rows before you chart anything. df.head() and df.describe() take seconds.
Correlation does not show cause. Ask what else could explain the pattern.
The median is a better typical value than the mean when the data has outliers.
Start bar chart axes at zero, or small differences will look large.
Keep the raw data untouched and do every cleaning step in code, so you can repeat it.
board-games: Teach a game by starting with how you win, then how a turn works.
With two six-sided dice, 7 is the most likely total and comes up one roll in six.
Sleeve cards for games you play often. It is cheaper than replacing a worn deck.
The best player count for a game is often not its maximum. Check before game night.
Play the first game with open hands so everyone learns the rules together.
